sections.name: Intro
sections.note: D minor. Atmosphere, a string bed and flute fragments. Almost nothing is happening, which is what makes everything later feel large.

sections.name: First theme
sections.note: The oboe takes the melody over the bed. Cello and bass arrive underneath and the harmony gets a floor.

sections.name: Growth
sections.note: More lanes join. Still no violins — the most obvious melodic voice is being withheld.

sections.name: First wave
sections.note: Violins finally enter, already mid-build. Ten lanes playing. In a two-minute cue this would be a reasonable place to end.

sections.name: Pull back
sections.note: Straight from the peak down to three lanes, and bar 35 is empty. The reset that makes the second half work.

sections.name: Rebuild
sections.note: Fragments return one at a time. The same material, thinner, moving forward faster than the first build did.

sections.name: Second build
sections.note: Four lanes to ten in six bars. The first build took sixteen; this one takes six, which is why it reads as urgent.

sections.name: Finale
sections.note: Full orchestra, densest bars in the piece, and the tonality has arrived on D Lydian. Same tonic as bar 1, opposite feeling.

roles.note: Sustained bed, no rhythm and no movement. It exists to be something for the flute to sit on.
Fragments rather than a line — short gestures in the gaps, establishing colour before any melody exists.
Wordless pad well below the strings. You feel it more than hear it.
Solo oboe takes the first real melody. Reedy and exposed, and it carries over the texture without needing volume.
The bed becomes functional harmony as the bass arrives — same sound, different job.
Enters with the bass to give the floating harmony a floor.
Root motion. The first time the piece has a bottom.
Quiet horn line answering the oboe in the gaps rather than doubling it.
Runs and figuration filling the space above the melody — movement without adding a third tune.
Cello moves from harmony to a real countermelody underneath the theme.
First percussion. Sparse accents marking the phrase ends.
Trombones and tuba thicken the bottom without changing the harmony.
Violins take the theme for the first time, twenty-four bars in, and arrive already in the middle of a build.
Doubling Violin I a third or an octave below — weight rather than a separate line.
Fast runs against the violin melody. Same register, different rhythm, so both stay audible.
Choir moves into the chord, adding body without adding attack.
Rhythm becomes structural rather than decorative.
Horns hold the middle of the chord and glue the woodwinds to the brass.
Everything strips back to a bed again. The contrast is the point.
A fragment of the theme, alone, as a reminder of where the piece came from.
Cello carries the theme in its singing register — the same tune, darker.
Sparse figuration returns first, as it did in the intro.
Inner harmony under the cello line, deliberately not the melody this time.
Pulse returns and starts pushing forward.
Theme back in the violins, higher and more insistent.
Low brass enters properly. From here the bottom never leaves.
Horn countermelody cutting across the violins — the pairing that makes the build feel heroic.
Choir doubles the harmony an octave up, widening everything.
Rhythmic drive accelerates into the finale.
Full-force theme, top of the register, D Lydian. The raised fourth is what makes it read as brighter than major.
Trumpets finally do real work — held back for fifty-five bars so their entry lands.
Runs at the very top, adding brilliance rather than notes you can follow.
Horns fill the middle of the chord, the thing that stops a tutti sounding hollow.
Full weight underneath. Trombones and tuba are what make the finale feel like size rather than volume.
Choir on the chord, and the most obvious signal that this is the destination.
Doubling the bass in octaves for definition at the bottom.
Root motion, octave below the cello.
Everything the percussion has been saving.
Doubling Violin I an octave below through the climax.
Reeds are inside the tutti rather than leading it — colour, not line.
